The structural cue is the root's movement from divine naming to human kinship, followed by the protection and reception of displaced women in 60:10-12. The divine adjectives supply beneficent care; kinship supplies the social form that such care can create. I infer that mercy can generate obligations analogous to kinship even when biological ties fail. The opening therefore reads not only as an invocation of compassion but as the enabling relation for a community reorganized around protected persons.

2. **Affection cast as actionable transmission.** ل ق ي B005 gives casting or placing something before another, and و د د B001 gives affection and attachment; the same مَوَدَّة is repeated after تُسِرُّونَ, whose س ر ر B001 supplies inward concealment and private communication. The casting image assigns affection the role of a transferred social signal, with secrecy serving as its channel. I infer that a concealed affective signal can enable the hostile expulsion already named in the ayah. The reading shifts from “feeling love” to covertly delivering attachment in a way that changes allegiance.

The ayah first names “My path” and closes with “the middle/equity of the path,” framing the intervening concealment as a route error.
